title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1973-11-10

ai_review.summary: Soundboard source with noticeable pitch/speed issues, but a stellar second‑set sandwich of Playin' > Uncle John's > Morning Dew makes the show worth listening to despite technical flaws.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard capture that suffers from speed/pitch problems and occasional level spikes, especially around the UJB section, requiring correction for comfortable listening. Musically the night shines in the second set – the deep Playin'‑Uncle John's‑Morning Dew sandwich, plus highlights like Jack Straw, Bertha, Big River, Stella Blue and a fiery Truckin'/Wharf Rat finish – even though the first set is viewed as uneven.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the second‑set performances and give 4–5 stars, while several note serious recording speed/pitch problems that drag the overall rating down, resulting in a solid but not outstanding score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Pitch runs high (≈½‑1 semitone) and speed is fast; noticeable wow & flutter on the SBD. Levels blow out during the UJB jam, and a few cuts are reported, but the overall mix is usable after pitch correction.

standout_songs: Playin' In The Band > Uncle John's Band > Morning Dew > Uncle John's Band > Playin'
poor_songs: First‑set songs that feel lackluster (e.g., Loser, early Bertha)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set is described as uneven and a bit lackluster, but the second set erupts into an intense, “pressure‑cooker” performance with a memorable jam sandwich that lifts the entire show.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly noted for raging, hot, masterful guitar work – especially his swirl in the Playin' sandwich and high energy on Jack Straw and Big River.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s cascading riffs get a shout‑out during Wharf Rat.
